clue.text: Pound notes may be what it means to a musician!

definitions.text: Pound notes may be what it means to a musician!

parts.words: Pound notes may be what it means to a musician!
parts.note: pound notes reads like banknotes, but to a musician it means hammering the notes out, the score marking for very loud playing

explanation.surface: A musician being told what a tip in sterling banknotes means to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound notes' looks like money; read 'pound' as a verb, to strike hard, and the notes are being played as loudly as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian score direction for very loud playing is exactly what pounding the notes produces.

clue.text: On top of the bowling unit

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.definitionFit: The word means above, and in cricket it is the set of six deliveries from one end.

clue.text: Pulling, we hear, on the line — or standing by?

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it is spoken, not by its spelling

parts.note: pulling a vehicle or boat behind is towing

explanation.surface: A tug pulling something on a line, or someone just standing waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the line' completes the idiom of toeing the line, conforming to the rules; standing by them is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Toeing the line means obeying the rules, which is standing by them loyally.

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
dining is eating

explanation.surface: A description of small chairs used at a dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small dining chairs' reads as one furniture description; it breaks into three jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats or chairs provided collectively for a venue are called by this word.

clue.text: I stand up to a Greek character

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word to is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to stand up to a Greek man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand up' turns TO into OT in a down entry. 'character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, the counterpart of our letter i.

indicators.note: posed means arranged into a position, so the letters of as Roman are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An artisan modelling while dressed up as an ancient Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft worker' suggests an artisan; the craft is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower works a boat, and a boat is a craft, so this is a craft worker.

clue.text: They act unthinkingly, placing plant needing warmth in a sickly sun

indicators.note: in means the plant is set inside the letters that come from a sickly sun
sickly means unwell or out of sorts, so the letters of sun are mixed up

parts.note: the tomato is a plant that needs warmth to ripen its fruit

explanation.surface: Mindless people put a warmth-loving plant out in a weak sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sickly' makes the anagram UNS. 'placing' is only a link word; the plant goes in after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Robots and machine-like people carry out actions mechanically, with no thought behind them.

clue.text: He'd a treaty drawn up, poised for action

indicators.note: drawn up means composed or set out, so the letters of he'd a treaty are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A diplomat had a treaty drafted and was ready to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn up' looks like drafting a document; it signals the rearrangement of HEDATREATY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being ready and in position, like a weapon held prepared for use.

definitions.meaning: informally, a firm that has gone ... is broke and has failed
a sculpture of a head and shoulders is a classic form of artwork

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as slang for broke and as the name for a sculpted head-and-shoulders piece.

clue.text: Patron that has been upset by agent

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the word been are tipped into a new order

parts.note: a factor is an agent who does business on another's behalf

explanation.surface: A patron who has been upset by some agent acting for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives the anagram BENE. A factor is an old word for a business agent, as on a Scottish estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron supports an artist or cause with money, as a generous donor or sponsor does.

clue.text: Yet such talkers may not be on the level

definitions.text: Yet such talkers may not be on the level

parts.words: Yet such talkers may not be on the level
parts.note: a word meaning level or even also describes a glib, persuasive talker, who may well not be honest

explanation.surface: A warning that slick, persuasive speakers may not be honest with you.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox: the word means flat or level, yet the talkers it describes are not 'on the level', meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib, plausible talkers are called by this word, which also means perfectly flat and even.

definitions.meaning: heavy weapons such as cannon and field pieces
brass hats is slang for senior officers or important people

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both heavy cannon and, figuratively, the most important people in an organisation.

parts.note: Snoopy looks like the Peanuts cartoon dog, but snoopy means nosy, so these are nosy, prying people

explanation.surface: The cast of the Peanuts strip featuring the dog Snoopy.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around 'Snoopy' hint that it is not the cartoon beagle but the adjective for prying.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy people who meddle in other folk's affairs are snoopers, characters who are snoopy.

parts.note: looks like idle chatter about trivial things, but means talking in broad terms with no specific cases

explanation.surface: Making small talk about nothing much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing in particular' suggests idle chat; read literally, it means avoiding particulars and speaking in broad terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak in sweeping terms, without specific examples, is to make broad statements.
The phrase can mean extremely remote, or up to this point in time.

clue.text: A month, just, in part of London

parts.note: the fifth month of the year is May
just means fair, as in a just or fair ruling

explanation.surface: Someone spending a month, or just about, in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' reads as 'only', but here it is the adjective meaning fair. Mayfair is an expensive district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of an exclusive, wealthy district in London's West End.

parts.note: looks like hearing news of something, but means words are heard coming out of this body part

explanation.surface: Someone getting to hear news about a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hears word of' usually means getting news; here the words literally come from it, the organ of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken words issue from this part of the face, so it is where one hears a word from.

parts.note: to travel is to go
a ton is British slang for a speed of a hundred miles per hour

explanation.surface: A motorist carried on driving at a hundred miles an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, 'doing a ton' means driving at 100mph.
explanation.definitionFit: To have carried on or continued with something is a synonym for having proceeded.

parts.note: a boy is a son
the middle letter of the word night, read as mid-night

explanation.surface: A lad goes out to take the night air at twelve o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is split as 'mid night', the middle letter of NIGHT. 'air' looks like the night breeze, but it means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple tune or melody, the musical sense of the word.

clue.text: English county shortly linking with a US state

parts.note: IOW is the short form of the Isle of Wight, an island county off England's south coast

explanation.surface: An English county briefly being twinned with an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an English island county, abbreviated IOW.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Midwestern American state whose capital is Des Moines.

definitions.meaning: read as a woman is: a female given name, one of the virtue names
a religion is a ... or creed someone holds

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a girl's given name and also means a system of religious belief.

clue.text: Fear led to model form of government

indicators.note: to model is to shape or fashion, so the letters of fear led are formed anew

explanation.surface: Fear prompted a particular model of government to be adopted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun for a system; it is the verb signalling the rearrangement of FEARLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A system in which states share power with a central authority is this kind of government.

clue.text: One saves, but it's more difficult with nothing coming in

indicators.note: coming in means the zero for nothing goes inside the word for more difficult

parts.note: more difficult means harder
O is nothing, the zero figure

explanation.surface: Someone saves, though with no income it grows harder.
explanation.walkthrough: The saver with nothing coming in sounds like hard times; 'coming in' puts O inside HARDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stockpiles things and keeps them laid away is a collector who saves.

definitions.meaning: a boom is a floating bar laid across a harbour or river to block it
a supersonic aircraft breaks the sound ..., which makes a sonic boom

explanation.definitionFit: A boom across a river is a barrier, and a jet going supersonic breaks the sound barrier.

definitions.meaning: the virtue of truthfulness and integrity
a garden plant with papery, coin-like seed pods, grown in gardens

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the virtue of truthfulness and also a garden plant, Lunaria, with silvery seed pods.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An order placed for frozen cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoin is to command or instruct someone formally, which is to order them.

parts.note: D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds
to duck something is to dodge or elude it

explanation.surface: A card player leads with a diamond, then ducks the next trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-table picture misleads: 'Lead on' is the definition, meaning to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to mislead or fool them, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Check caught and bowled, with interruption by game being held up

indicators.note: interruption by means the game's letters break into the pair from caught and bowled

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: in a down clue, being held up means the game is read upwards

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard check: caught and bowled, with play delayed by another game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being held up' turns the game upwards in this down entry, and 'with interruption by' puts it between the two cricket letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb something is to restrain or hold it back, a synonym of check.

indicators.note: of says the letters come from within the word Spithead

explanation.surface: Pointing to the key part of Spithead, the naval anchorage.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is a stretch of water off Portsmouth, long used as a Royal Navy anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith of a matter is its core or essence, its most important part.

definitions.meaning: Robin Hood's merry men would gather around their leader Robin
a petition whose signatures are written in a circle so no one name heads the list

explanation.definitionFit: Hood's outlaws gathered round Robin, and a petition signed in a ring hides who signed first.

clue.text: Gaelic verses with no beginning or end

indicators.note: the word verses loses its first and its last letter, keeping only the middle

explanation.surface: Gaelic poetry that has neither a start nor a finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no beginning or end' strips the V and the final S from VERSES.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Settings for old stories with misleading passages

definitions.text: Settings for old stories with misleading passages

parts.words: Settings for old stories with misleading passages
parts.note: misleading passages looks like deceptive bits of text, but means confusing corridors, mazes such as the Minotaur's on Crete in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Old tales whose sections of text are deliberately deceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passages' tempts toward written extracts; they are corridors, as in the Cretan maze of the Minotaur myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazes of confusing corridors, like the one built for the Minotaur, feature as settings in ancient myths.
